mex:Work Orders (Work Orders & Inspectio.purpose: The MEX Work Order module is the maintenance job-management area. It records work to be done on an Asset (or work already done): instructions, required spare parts and materials, labour (people, trades, estimated and actual time), photos and documents, and key dates (raised, due start, started, completed). It has two record types, standard Work Orders and Work Order Inspections, which are worked through in the mobile app. The landing page states that a Work Order can be used simply to record work already done. Sources are the help guide pages read below, all dated November 2023. The guide does not describe approvals, report output, or the full list of status values, so those parts are not covered here.

features.name: Work Order creation
features.description: A new Work Order can be raised from the + button on the bottom menu, available from any app screen. An Asset and a description are mandatory to save. Other details are optional and the record is saved by leaving the form.

features.name: Work Order Listing
features.description: The main screen for managing outstanding Work Orders, reached from the bottom Work Orders button or from sort buttons on the Home screen.

features.description: Predefined sorts: My Work, Date Specific, Statuses and Trade Filters. An active sort can be cleared.

features.name: Full filter
features.description: Filter by Work Order number, status, group Work Order, account code, Asset (with include-children option), priority, dates raised / due start / finished, description, component code, job type, department, trade code and name, contractor, and raised-by. Filters can be reset.

features.name: Listing sort options
features.description: Sort by due date, due finish date, Work Order number, priority (each ascending or descending), Asset number, or job type.

features.name: Standard Work Order details
features.description: Single-job view showing the Work Order number, priority, due date, estimated hours, Asset (with hierarchy and asset identity details and parent asset), total time spent, photos, instructions, tasks, parts, history notes, signature, and customer/quote/order references.

features.name: Job timer
features.description: A clock control starts a timer for the current user, provided a trade is assigned to that user. Elapsed time is written to the actual time under the trades section.

features.name: Photos and documents
features.description: Photos can be captured directly in the app and saved to the MEX system. Associated documents are attached as external files and can be printed with the Work Order.

features.name: Parts issue from job
features.description: Parts listed on the Work Order open the spare parts form, where they can be issued.

features.name: Work Order Inspection details
features.description: Inspection jobs list many Assets. Each row shows asset number, description, number of questions, questions answered, percentage complete, and picture. A search bar finds a specific Asset. Overall progress is shown at the top and updates as each inspection is completed.

features.name: Inspection sorting and filters
features.description: Predefined filters: Incomplete inspections, Exceptions, and Not Approved inspections, plus a full filter.

records: Work Order (standard): Work Order Number, Priority, Due Date/Due Start, Due Finish, Estimated Hours, Status, Raised By, Asset (number, description, parent, hierarchy, manufacturer, model, serial, registration), Instructions, Tasks, Parts, Labour/Trades with estimated and actual time, Photos and external documents, History Notes, Signature, Customer name, Quote number and amount, Order number, Job Type, Department, Contractor, Group Work Order, Account Code, Component Code. Dates: raised, due start, started, completed.

Work Order Inspection: a single job covering multiple Assets. Each Asset entry has Asset number, description, question count, answered count, percentage complete, and picture. Inspections can be marked Incomplete, Exception, or Not Approved.
Spare part requirement: a line on a Work Order that links to the spare parts issue form.
workflows: Technicians open a Work Order from the listing, start the job timer under their assigned trade, capture photos, work through tasks and instructions, issue listed parts, and complete the record with a signature.
For inspections, the worker goes through the list of Assets, answering questions for each one. Filters show incomplete, exception and not-approved items. Progress updates as each Asset is completed.
Approvals and the exact status lifecycle (value names and transitions) are referenced by the guide (Status field, Not Approved filter) but are not described in the pages read.
reports: No reports are described in the pages read. The guide only mentions that Work Orders and their attached documents can be printed.

mex:Job Requests (Requests).purpose: The Requests module of the MEX maintenance system (MEX User Guide, helpguide.mex.com.au/app/requests/) lets personnel submit requests for maintenance work to the Maintenance Department. Maintenance can turn approved requests into Work Orders, and requesters can track progress without contacting maintenance directly. Approval gates the process: a request that is not authorised cannot become a Work Order. The page was fetched successfully (HTTP 200), and the three sub-pages it links to (Request Listing, Request Details, Creating a New Request) were also read. The guide is a 2023 user guide, so the description reflects that version.

features.name: Request submission
features.description: A request can be raised from the MEX app (the + button, then request), from the MEX main application, or from the MEX Ops web page. Only a description is required. Optional inputs are the asset (entered or searched), photos (uploaded or taken on the device), and priority. Priority carries over to any Work Order created from the request. Other details can be added after creation.

features.name: Approval notification and decision
features.description: When a request is entered, an email notification goes to the people who must approve it. An authorised user can approve or decline either by using the approve or decline link in that email or inside the Requests module. Approval is required before a Work Order can be generated.

features.name: Request Listing
features.description: The main screen of the module, reached from Your Dashboard (Your Requests or Requests Needing Approval), the bottom menu, or the hamburger menu. By default it shows outstanding requests: those not completed, not cancelled or declined, and those attached to a Work Order that is still open. Sort options are My Requests, Requests that Need Approval, and Status. Each row shows a preview with the description, who raised it, its picture, and how many other active requests exist for the same asset.

features.name: Request Details
features.description: Opened by tapping a request. Sections cover a preview header (description, raised date and time, who raised it, status, picture), the actions available (Approve, Create Work Order, Decline), the asset number and description with an asset-tree and equipment detail popup (manufacturer, model, serial, registration), an Outstanding Work list of open Work Orders and requests for the same asset so a new request can be added to an existing job, a Notes section, and Photos. Administrators can chat with the requester through the notes.

features.name: Add to existing Work Order
features.description: If a Work Order already exists for the asset and fixes the problem, the request can be attached to that job instead of creating a new one.

features.name: Completion and automatic closure
features.description: When the linked Work Order is closed to History, the request closes itself as completed. The requester can be notified by email automatically.

features.name: Progress tracking by requester
features.description: Requesters can open the request list at any time to check the status of their own requests, which removes the need to chase maintenance for updates regardless of which entry channel they used.

records: Request: description (required), raised date and time, raised by (requester), status, picture/photos, priority, asset (optional link to an asset and its tree, manufacturer, model number, serial number, registration number), notes, linked Work Order (if any), approval state (approved, declined, cancelled, or completed as described in the listing rules).
workflows: 1. Requester enters a Maintenance Request (app, main application, or MEX Ops web page). 2. Email notification goes to the approvers. 3. Approver approves or declines, via the email link or in the Requests module. A declined or cancelled request is not listed as outstanding. 4. Once approved, maintenance staff generate a Work Order from the request, or attach it to an existing open Work Order for the same asset. 5. Maintenance completes the Work Order as usual. 6. When the Work Order is closed to History, the request closes as completed and the requester can be emailed. Statuses seen in the guide: outstanding, approved, declined, cancelled, completed, and attached to an open Work Order.
reports: The guide does not describe any dedicated reports for the Requests module. Its screens are the Request Listing (with sort views) and the Request Details screen.

mex:Stocktakes.purpose: Stocktakes in MEX confirm that physical stock on the shelf matches the quantity recorded in MEX, and adjust the Catalogue Stock on Hand values to the counted figures where they differ. Differences arise from unprocessed movements, goods received but not yet shelved, items put in the wrong location, and quantities issued to a Work Order or Account Code that differ from what was physically taken. A stocktake runs in three stages: creation in the main MEX product, counting (on paper or a mobile device, optionally with barcode scanning), and processing by a user with appropriate authority. The three pages read were the index (https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/stocktake/), Stocktake Listing (https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/stocktake-listing/) and Stocktake Details (https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/stocktake-details/). All were fetched successfully (HTTP 200). The guide is from 2023 and is brief, so details such as permissions, approval steps, and creation screens are not covered.

features.name: Re-order items

features.name: Scan to find item

features.name: Type-to-search catalogue item

features.name: Count entry per item

mex:Readings.purpose: The MEX Readings module records readings taken from an Asset (hour meters, odometers, pressure gauges, shock pulse meters, or any other instrument the user needs to track asset performance). Readings are entered in the field, mainly through the mobile app. Each reading must be tied to an Asset Number from the Asset Register, a date/time, and a Reading Type. Readings are split into two kinds: usage-based readings, which can drive Routine Maintenance scheduling, and condition-monitoring readings, which report on asset condition and performance. Fetched from the overview page (https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/readings/, HTTP 200) and the Readings Listing page (https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/readings-listing/, HTTP 200). Both pages are from a non-preapproved source and are summarised here in my own words. The page on Asset Searching is the same URL with an anchor (#AssetSearch) and was not fetched separately.

features.name: Readings Listing (main screen)
features.description: The main Readings screen in the app, opened from the hamburger menu. It lists every reading the user can currently update, and a new reading can be entered and processed directly from it.

features.name: Asset search by barcode or QR code
features.description: The user scans an Asset's barcode or QR code to find the asset, then enters the reading. The reading is saved straight away and is ready for use in planned maintenance (PMs).

features.name: Per-reading entry row
features.description: Each listed reading shows the Asset Number, Asset Description, the time the last reading was taken, the last reading value, the Reading Type, and a text field for entering a new value.

features.name: Usage-based readings
features.description: Readings of asset usage such as operating hours or kilometres travelled. Once entered, they can be used to schedule Routine Maintenance.

features.name: Condition-monitoring readings
features.description: General readings such as temperatures, pressures or clearances, used to record and report on asset condition and performance.

features.name: Field entry on the go
features.description: The module is designed so users in the field can enter all their readings while working, without going back to a desk.

records: Reading: linked to an Asset Number from the Asset Register (required); has a Date/Time the reading was recorded (required); has a Reading Type (required, e.g. Exhaust Temperature, Operating Hours); has the reading value. Classed as Usage Based or Condition Monitoring.
Reading Type: defines what the reading measures. Each reading carries one.
Asset (from the Asset Register): identified by Asset Number and Asset Description; the last reading time and last reading value are shown against it in the listing.
workflows: Field user scans an asset's barcode or QR code, enters the reading value in the listing, and it is saved immediately for use by planned maintenance.
The two reading kinds feed different uses: usage-based readings feed Routine Maintenance scheduling; condition-monitoring readings are for recording and reporting condition and performance.
The pages describe no statuses, approval steps, or role-based responsibilities for readings.
reports: No reports are described on either page. The condition-monitoring readings are said to support reporting on asset condition and performance, but no named report is given.
subpages: https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/readings-listing/#AssetSearch (Readings & Asset Searching section; same page as the Readings Listing, not fetched separately)

mex:Edit Mode.purpose: Edit Mode is an administration tool inside the MEX App (also described as available on the MEX App) for configuring how screens behave for different security groups and for adjusting labels and forms. Only an administrator can use it: the user must not be assigned to any security group. Fetched from https://helpguide.mex.com.au/app/edit-mode/ (HTTP 200, page dated November 13, 2023). The overview page itself is brief and lists four capabilities, all of which are covered by sub-pages I also read.

features.name: Edit Security (field access per security group)
features.description: Per security group, set how each field on a screen is treated: Set Not Visible, Set Disabled, Read Only, or Clear. Changes are applied by tapping an option and then tapping fields on the form, which are colour-highlighted to confirm. Edit Mode is closed to save.

features.name: Mandatory fields
features.description: Per security group, mark fields on a form as mandatory using three options: Clear, Zero value allowed, or Zero value not allowed. Multiple fields can be set by dragging across them. Closing Edit Mode saves.

features.name: Change labels (Change Names)
features.description: Renames labels on the current screen. All adjustable labels are shown in a wiggle state; the user taps a label, types the new text and taps Done. Changed labels are shown in red as a visual indicator. Closing Edit Mode saves and the new label appears in listings.

features.name: Tailor listings and forms (custom fields)
features.description: The overview says listings and forms can be adapted to the user's specifications. The linked custom-fields page was not read, so details are not confirmed here.

records: Security group selection: the per-group context that Edit Security and Mandatory Fields settings apply to (no separate record fields documented).
Field-level security setting per field per security group: values Not Visible, Disabled, Read Only, Clear.
Field-level mandatory setting per field per security group: values Clear, Zero value allowed, Zero value not allowed.
Label override per label on a screen: the new label text, shown in red once changed.
No record types, notable fields or database objects are described on the pages read.
workflows: Administrator opens the app screen to change, opens the hamburger menu, taps Edit Mode, then chooses Security, Mandatory fields, or Change Names.
Security workflow: select a security group, choose one of the four security options, tap fields to apply, then close Edit Mode to save.
Mandatory fields workflow: select a security group, choose Clear / Zero value allowed / Zero value not allowed, tap or drag across fields, then close Edit Mode to save.
Change names workflow: tap Change Names, tap a label, enter new text, tap Done, then close Edit Mode to save.
No approval or status workflow is described. Changes take effect on closing Edit Mode.
reports: None described on the pages read.

code:assets.area: Assets: asset register, hierarchy, CSV import, specifications, criticality, status, strategy, sites, QR labels and scanning, asset page extras (BIZOMAT ERP Maintenance, stages M1 to M3)

features.name: Asset register record (fields and storage)
features.what: One row per asset per company. Fields: number, name, description, category, type, manufacturer, model, serial_number, registration_number, purchase_date, commissioning_date, warranty_until, supplier, purchase_cost_cents, replacement_cost_cents, location (free text), department (free text) or department_id (a co_departments row), responsible_id (a user), criticality, status, strategy, specs_json, parent_id, a search column, archived_at, created_by/at, updated_at. Costs are whole cents (>= 0, up to 1e13). Every query filters on company_id, and (company_id, id) foreign keys stop a link to another company's asset. assetDTO joins department name, responsible name, parent number/name and the site (code/name).
features.evidence: apps/work/migrations/0018_maintenance.sql (CREATE TABLE mt_assets, unique index mt_assets_number(company_id, number), mt_assets_parent, mt_assets_serial); apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/routes-assets.ts (SELECT const, assetDTO, loadAsset, fields/createSchema/updateSchema, columnsOf)
features.limits: No custom fields beyond the free-form specs. Category and type are free text, with no managed list or asset classes. Location is free text, separate from sites. Costs are for information only: no depreciation, no book value, nothing posted to Finance. No barcode or RFID field other than the QR label made from the number.

features.name: Asset numbering
features.what: A number given by hand must match ASSET_NUMBER_RE (letters, digits and . _ / -, up to 40 characters) and be unique in the company (case-insensitive, 409 otherwise). With no number given, the next A-0001-style number comes from mt_counters. The counter first moves past the highest A-<digits> number already in the company (numbers given by hand or imported), so it never repeats one. The import takes a block of numbers in one call.
features.evidence: apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/util.ts (NUMBERING asset prefix 'A-' width 4, nextNumbers, ASSET_NUMBER_RE); apps/work/migrations/0018_maintenance.sql (mt_counters); routes-assets.ts validate() and POST /c/:company/assets
features.limits: The prefix and width are fixed (A-, 4 digits), with no per-company or per-category number format. A number can be changed later on edit, and the QR label changes with it, because the label encodes the number.

features.name: Create, edit, archive and restore assets
features.what: POST /assets creates an asset (supervisor or admin) and PATCH /assets/:id changes only the fields given. validate() checks: number format and uniqueness; no duplicate manufacturer plus serial number (case-insensitive, checked only when either field changes); a parent in the same company that is not the asset itself or one below it (assetPath, recursive CTE, depth 200); department_id only for registered companies (others type the department); the responsible person is in the company (assertPerson, at least requester). The search text is rebuilt from number, name, manufacturer, model, serial, registration, location, category and type. Each change writes mt_events ('asset.created' or 'asset.updated' with the before and after diff from changes()). POST /assets/:id/archive and /restore set or clear archived_at with an event ('asset.archived' or 'asset.restored'). The client's AssetFormDialog has sections for the asset, make and identity, purchase and warranty, place and people, maintenance (criticality, status, strategy) and specifications. Its parent picker is AssetPicker, which leaves out the asset itself. 'Add one' under 'Assets under it' opens the form with the parent filled in. Archiving asks for confirmation.
features.evidence: apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/routes-assets.ts (assetRoutes.post '/c/:company/assets', patch '/c/:company/assets/:id', the archive/restore loop, validate, searchOf); apps/work/src/client/system/maintenance/Assets.tsx (AssetFormDialog, AssetDetail archive(), toCents/dollars); pickers.tsx (AssetPicker, DepartmentField, PersonSelect); index.ts me.can.manageAssets = isManager
features.limits: Assets cannot be deleted, only archived. Archiving does not cascade to the assets under it and does not check open work orders or PM schedules. No bulk edit, bulk archive or bulk re-parent. The edit form has no site field (the site is set separately on the asset page). A parent that is archived is accepted by the API, though the picker offers only assets in use. Changing the parent does not change the site. Requesters and technicians can only view.

features.name: Hierarchy (tree of any depth)
features.what: parent_id links an asset under another asset of the company, to any depth. Loops are refused on the server. GET /assets/tree returns up to 5,000 nodes (in use only, or all with archived=all), each with its status, criticality, category and the count of outstanding work orders the caller may see (workOrderScope). The client Hierarchy tab builds the tree, with expand and collapse per node, Expand all and Collapse all, 'Show archived', and badges (Archived, a status other than operating, high or critical criticality, 'N open', 'N under it'). Searching by number, name or category on the client shows each match with every asset above it. The asset page shows the breadcrumb path from the root (assetPath) and lists its direct children (up to 500, each with its own child count). SUBTREE_SQL (recursive, depth 200) gives an asset and everything under it, for site placement and the work order filter with includeChildren.
features.evidence: routes-assets.ts (GET '/c/:company/assets/tree', assetPath, SUBTREE_SQL, children query in GET '/c/:company/assets/:id'); Assets.tsx (AssetTree, TreeNode, the mt-path nav, the 'Assets under it' section); 0018_maintenance.sql FOREIGN KEY (company_id, parent_id)
features.limits: No drag-and-drop re-parenting: an asset moves by editing its parent. The tree is capped at 5,000 nodes and renders 60 levels deep on the client. Tree search runs on the client over number, name and category only. Costs, downtime and work do not roll up the hierarchy on the asset page. No functional location versus equipment distinction and no positions or slots.

features.name: Asset list with filters
features.what: GET /assets filters by archived (in use, archived or all), q (LIKE on the search column), status, criticality, strategy, category (case-insensitive), siteId (a site, or 'none' for assets not in a site) and parent ('root' or an id). It sorts by number, name or recently changed, with limit (default 200, max 1,000) and offset. It returns the total and the company's distinct categories (up to 200). The client List tab keeps the filters in the URL and shows Number, Name, Category, Make and model, Site and location, Status, Criticality and Under (the parent). It says 'Showing X of Y' when there are more.
features.evidence: routes-assets.ts (assetRoutes.get '/c/:company/assets'); Assets.tsx (AssetList, FilterPanel use); util.ts likeOf/searchText
features.limits: The UI has no paging (offset is supported by the API but not used), no column choice, no CSV or Excel export of the register, no saved views and no filter on department, responsible person, manufacturer, warranty or specification values. Search does not cover specifications or description.

features.name: Asset page (detail)
features.what: GET /assets/:id returns: the asset; its path; its parent; its children; outstanding work orders on it (in the caller's scope, by due date, up to 200); open requests on it (in the caller's request scope, up to 200); history from mt_events (up to 200, without lines about requests or work orders the caller cannot see); files (mt_files); the extras (meters, schedules, prestart template, prestarts, qrUrl); and can.edit and can.upload (supervisor or admin). The screen shows the header with status, criticality and archived badges, plus Report a fault, New work order (managers), Edit and Archive/Restore. The side column has About, Site and label, Meters and gauges, Purchase and warranty (with '(ended)' when the warranty date has passed) and Technical specifications. The main column has Outstanding work (with a link to the work orders of the assets under it), Preventive maintenance, Prestart checks, Open requests, Assets under it, Photos and documents (upload and remove for managers) and Maintenance history.
features.evidence: routes-assets.ts (assetRoutes.get '/c/:company/assets/:id'); asset-extras.ts (assetExtras); Assets.tsx (AssetDetail, AssetView, AssetDetailData); routes-files.ts parentOf (asset files: managers only); util.ts filesOf
features.limits: No cost summary (labour, parts or downtime totals) and no reliability figures (MTBF, MTTR) on the page; those are in Reports. No closed work order list on the page, only outstanding ones plus the history. Warranty is shown but nothing alerts before it ends. No status history view other than the event lines.

features.name: Technical specifications
features.what: Up to 60 key and value pairs per asset (key 1 to 80 characters, value up to 500), stored as JSON in specs_json. They are edited as lines in the asset form, shown as a property list on the asset page and imported from 'Spec: <name>' CSV columns.
features.evidence: routes-assets.ts (spec schema, specs: z.array(spec).max(60), columnsOf specs_json); csv.ts (spec: columns in planImport); Assets.tsx (Technical specifications fieldset and section); 0018_maintenance.sql specs_json
features.limits: Free-form text only: no units, number types, templates per category or class, or required specifications. Specifications are not searchable or filterable, and assets cannot be compared by them.

features.name: Criticality
features.what: An enum per asset: low, medium (default), high, critical. It is set in the form or the import, is a list filter, is shown as a badge (CriticalityBadge) and is flagged in the tree for high and critical. It is returned by the scan lookup.
features.evidence: util.ts CRITICALITY; 0018_maintenance.sql CHECK on criticality; routes-assets.ts list filter; Assets.tsx (CriticalityBadge in tree, list and detail); routes-setup.ts scan response
features.limits: A label only. Nothing else in the maintenance server reads it (no grep hit outside the asset routes and the scan): it does not set request or work order priority, PM, or report weighting. No risk matrix or scored criticality assessment (consequence times likelihood), and no history of criticality decisions other than event diffs.

features.name: Operating status
features.what: An enum per asset: operating (default), standby, under_maintenance, out_of_service, disposed. It is set by hand in the form or the import, filtered in the list, shown as a badge, and in the tree when not operating. The overview counts assets 'down' (under_maintenance or out_of_service). The only automatic change is a prestart check with a failed critical item, which sets the asset to out_of_service (unless it is already out of service or disposed) and records an 'asset.out_of_service' event with the status before.
features.evidence: util.ts ASSET_STATUS; 0018_maintenance.sql CHECK on status; routes-inspections.ts (outOfService and UPDATE mt_assets SET status = 'out_of_service', around lines 435-453); index.ts overview 'down' count; Assets.tsx AssetStatusBadge
features.limits: Work orders and downtime records do not change the status, and nothing returns an asset to operating automatically. 'disposed' is only a status: there is no disposal record (date, method or value), and disposed assets stay in the register unless archived. No separate status history table (only mt_events).

features.name: Maintenance strategy
features.what: An enum per asset: run_to_failure (default), preventive, condition_based, predictive. It is set in the form or the import, is a list filter and is shown on the asset page.
features.evidence: util.ts STRATEGY; 0018_maintenance.sql CHECK on strategy; routes-assets.ts list filter; Assets.tsx STRATEGY_LABELS
features.limits: Informational only. Nothing else reads it: it does not create or require PM schedules or meters.

features.name: Department and responsible person
features.what: A registered company's asset may name a co_departments row (department_id), and the name is shown. Other companies type a department. A responsible person must be a person of the company.
features.evidence: routes-assets.ts validate() (departmentName, assertPerson 'requester'); SELECT joins co_departments and users; pickers.tsx DepartmentField and PersonSelect
features.limits: One responsible person per asset. No team or crew, and nobody is notified. The import takes the department only as text (no department_id, no responsible person).

features.name: CSV import with preview (dry run)
features.what: POST /assets/import (maintenance admin only, rate limit 20 a minute per user) takes CSV text of up to 2 MB, with dryRun true by default. parseCsv follows RFC 4180 (quotes, CRLF or LF, BOM stripped, blank lines skipped). Headers are matched to fields without case or punctuation, with synonyms (for example make or brand for manufacturer, rego for registration, 'site' or 'area' for location, parent or parentnumber), and a field named twice counts only its first column. 'Spec: <name>' columns become specifications. Each row is validated: name required, text length limits, dates as YYYY-MM-DD or day-first DD/MM/YYYY (csvDate), money as '$1,234.50' or 'AUD' (csvCents), and criticality, status and strategy codes, with defaults medium, operating and run_to_failure. A row whose number, or manufacturer plus serial, is already in the register or earlier in the file is a duplicate. Parents are resolved by number, to an existing asset or a row of the file. Rows whose parent fails, or whose parents loop, become errors, repeated until nothing changes. The preview returns the column mapping, each row's line, status and messages, and a summary. The import inserts parents before children (importOrder) in batches of 200 statements, auto-numbers rows without a number, and writes an 'asset.imported' event per asset plus one 'assets.imported' summary event. The client's ImportDialog takes a file chooser (2 MB check) or pasted text, offers 'Use an example', a Preview button, then 'Import N assets', and shows a results table (Ready, Duplicate, Error, Imported) with the unused columns.
features.evidence: apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/csv.ts (parseCsv, COLUMNS, LIMITS, csvDate, csvCents, planImport, importOrder, MAX_IMPORT_ROWS = 2000, MAX_IMPORT_BYTES = 2 MiB); routes-assets.ts (assetRoutes.post '/c/:company/assets/import'); Assets.tsx (ImportDialog, SAMPLE, ImportResult); index.ts me.can.importAssets = admin; test-node/maintenance.test.ts
features.limits: Creates new assets only. No update or upsert of existing assets: matches are skipped as duplicates. It cannot set a site (mt_asset_sites), department_id, responsible person or files, and a 'Site' header goes to the free-text location. Rows past 2,000 are dropped silently (table.slice) with no message. Dates are day-first only for the slash form. The batches of 200 are separate transactions, so a failure part-way can leave a partial import. No import of meters, PM or readings, no export or template download other than the example, and no XLSX.

features.name: Sites and placing assets in a site
features.what: mt_sites (code unique per company, matching CODE_RE; name, address, notes, archived_at) and the side table mt_asset_sites (one site per asset, set_by and set_at), so mt_assets is unchanged. GET /sites lists up to 500 sites, each with its count of assets in use, plus the count of assets not in a site and can.manage. POST /sites and PATCH /sites/:id (code, name, address, notes, archived) are for supervisors and admins and write 'site.created' or 'site.updated' events. PUT /assets/:id/site places an asset, and optionally every asset under it (SUBTREE_SQL), in a site or takes it out, in batches of 100, with an 'asset.site' event. A new asset takes the given siteId or, failing that, its parent's site. PATCH /assets/:id also accepts siteId. assertSite refuses another company's site or an archived one. inSiteSql filters assets (and, elsewhere, lists, the calendar and reports) by site. Client: Settings > Sites (a table of code, name and address, asset counts, Archive/Restore, an add form with code, name and address, and the unplaced count); the asset page's SiteField select with 'With the assets under it'; the asset list's site filter (including 'Not in a site'); the labels page's site filter.
features.evidence: apps/work/migrations/0024_maintenance_m2_m3.sql (mt_sites, mt_sites_code, mt_asset_sites, mt_asset_sites_site); routes-setup.ts (GET/POST '/c/:company/sites', PATCH '/c/:company/sites/:id', PUT '/c/:company/assets/:id/site', siteDTO); m2util.ts (assertSite, inSiteSql); routes-assets.ts (create site inheritance, PATCH siteId branch, siteId list filter); Setup.tsx (SitesSection); AssetExtras.tsx (SiteField); Maintenance.tsx Settings
features.limits: Sites are flat: no site hierarchy, regions or areas, and a site is not an asset. No map, GPS or geolocation. The UI cannot rename a site or edit its address or notes after it is made (the API can), and notes cannot be entered in the UI at all. Archiving a site leaves its assets in it. Moving an asset to a new parent does not move its site. Sites are not linked to WHS sites, ERP warehouses or company addresses. The import cannot place assets in sites.

features.name: QR labels
features.what: GET /assets/:id/qr returns an SVG QR code encoding 'ASSET:<number>' with a caption of the number and name (up to 60 characters), made by the ERP's own encoder (no third-party service, error correction level M, up to 213 bytes), served private, cached for 5 minutes, with a strict CSP. The asset page shows the label (QrLabel) and a 'Print this label' link. The Labels page (/maintenance/labels) shows a sheet of labels for the assets in use (up to 500 from /assets), filtered by site or ?ids=, and prints it with window.print().
features.evidence: routes-setup.ts (assetCode, setupRoutes.get '/c/:company/assets/:id/qr'); apps/work/src/worker/erp/qr.ts (qrSvg, QR_MAX_BYTES); asset-extras.ts qrUrl; AssetExtras.tsx (QrLabel); Field.tsx (LabelsPage); Maintenance.tsx route 'labels'
features.limits: The code holds the asset number, not a URL, so a phone's own camera app will not open the ERP; it must be scanned in the ERP's Scan screen. Renumbering an asset makes old printed labels stale. No label sizes or templates, no linear barcode output, no PDF, and no choosing many assets in the UI (only all, a site, or the ids parameter from one asset's link). Archived assets and assets past the first 500 are not offered.

features.name: Scan or type an asset code
features.what: GET /scan?code= (anyone with access) strips an 'ASSET:' prefix and finds the asset by number (case-insensitive), then by serial number, then by registration number, preferring assets in use for the last two. It returns the asset summary (number, name, status, criticality, archived, location), its prestart checklist (template not archived) and the count of outstanding work orders the caller may see. 404 when nothing matches. The Scan screen (phone layout) has a code field, plus a camera reader where the browser has BarcodeDetector and getUserMedia (QR, Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, rear camera, a frame every 350 ms). The result card offers Prestart check (when a checklist is set), Report a fault and Open the asset. The same CodeField is used to pick the asset on the Prestart screen.
features.evidence: routes-setup.ts (setupRoutes.get '/c/:company/scan'); Field.tsx (CameraReader, CodeField, ScanPage, PrestartPage); Maintenance.tsx route 'scan' and the Overview 'Scan an asset' button
features.limits: The camera works only in browsers with BarcodeDetector (not all browsers); otherwise the code is typed. Requires sign-in and network (no offline mode; offline field work is listed as planned in Settings). It does not jump straight to the asset. It finds the first match only and cannot choose between duplicate serials. It cannot look up meters, parts or work orders.

features.name: Asset page extras from M2 and M3 (asset-extras.ts)
features.what: assetExtras() adds to the asset page: the asset's meters and gauges (mt_meters, meterDTO), its PM schedules (loadSchedulesOfAsset), its prestart checklist (mt_asset_prestart joined to mt_insp_templates), the 10 latest prestarts (mt_prestarts: result, template, failed items, set out of service, when, by whom) and qrUrl. Client: MetersSection (add a meter or gauge with unit, kind, rollover and expected minimum and maximum; enter a reading with a reset flag, which may generate PM work orders; open the readings history; archive a meter); PreventiveOfAsset (the schedules with trigger, next due and paused, and a link to schedule new PM); PrestartOfAsset (a manager sets or clears the checklist through PUT /assets/:id/prestart; a 'Do a check' link; the latest results with 'Set out of service'); QrLabel; SiteField.
features.evidence: apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/asset-extras.ts; routes-meters.ts (meterDTO, POST /meters, POST /meters/:id/readings, GET/PATCH /meters/:id); pm.ts loadSchedulesOfAsset; routes-inspections.ts (PUT/GET '/c/:company/assets/:id/prestart'); apps/work/src/client/system/maintenance/AssetExtras.tsx (MetersSection, AddMeter, MeterReadings, PreventiveOfAsset, PrestartOfAsset, QrLabel, SiteField)
features.limits: One prestart checklist per asset. Only the 10 latest prestarts on the page. Archived meters are left out of the section. The meter and PM logic lives in other areas' files; this file only gathers them for the asset page.

features.name: Asset files (photos and documents)
features.what: Files attached to an asset (mt_files, asset_id) in the app's file store, up to 25 MB each through validateUpload, rate limited to 60 a minute. Only supervisors and admins add or remove an asset's files. Each change is recorded in mt_events. Images and PDFs open inline. Listed on the asset page under Photos and documents.
features.evidence: 0018_maintenance.sql (mt_files with its CHECK of exactly one parent); routes-files.ts (parentOf asset_id branch, POST '/c/:company/files', MAX_FILE_BYTES from worker/routes/files.ts = 25 MiB); util.ts filesOf; Assets.tsx (UploadButton, FileList)
features.limits: No document types, expiry dates, versions or a library shared between assets. Technicians cannot attach files to an asset directly (only to their work orders).

code:work.area: Maintenance: requests and work orders (request approval, work order lifecycle, tasks, labour timer and manual time, trades, labour rates and costs, comments, files, downtime, completion, reopening, history). API under /api/maintenance (mounted in /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/index.ts); screens under /erp/c/<company>/maintenance (routes in /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/src/client/system/maintenance/Maintenance.tsx). Tables from /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/migrations/0018_maintenance.sql (Stage 1) and 0024_maintenance_m2_m3.sql (M2/M3). Tests: apps/work/test/maintenance.test.ts, maintenance-m2-m3.test.ts, test-node/ counterparts. Things missing across the whole area: no notifications or email in the maintenance worker (grep finds no notify or send call); no CSV export of the request or work order lists (only the backlog report has a CSV); no printable work order or PDF; requests and work orders cannot be deleted; no offline mode.

features.name: Access, roles and record visibility
features.what: Each company has four maintenance roles, ranked requester < technician < supervisor < admin. Defaults: the owner and company admins are maintenance admins, other members are requesters, and the owner is always admin. A personal company and the example company make their owner the admin. requireMt resolves the company in the address and answers 404 to outsiders. isManager means supervisor or above. requestScope: managers see all requests, technicians see their own plus those on their assigned work orders, requesters see only their own. workOrderScope: managers see all work orders, technicians see those assigned to them, requesters see work orders made from their requests (read only). canWork: managers, or the technician the work order is assigned to. A suspended registered company answers 423.
features.evidence: /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/access.ts (MT_ROLES, effectiveRole, loadMtAccess, requireMt, isManager, requestScope, workOrderScope, assertPerson, mtCompanies); table mt_roles; /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/routes-work.ts canWork/assertWork; GET /api/maintenance/c/:company/me returns the can.* flags (index.ts)
features.limits: Access is one role per person per company, with no per-site, per-department or per-trade scoping. Only one technician can be assigned, so other technicians cannot work on or see a work order unless they are managers. No contractor or guest access. Removing a member reassigns their open work orders (company/members-routes.ts line ~362) with a direct UPDATE and writes no mt_events history line.

features.name: Request approval rule (company setting)
features.what: There is one setting per company, mt_settings.require_approval, default on (1). When it is on, new requests start as awaiting_approval; when off, they start as submitted. Only maintenance admins change it (PATCH /settings, event settings.changed). The same rule applies to requests raised by failed prestart checks and failed inspections.
features.evidence: routes-requests.ts requireApproval(); index.ts PATCH /c/:company/settings; client Maintenance.tsx Settings Switch 'New requests need approval' (lines ~233-251); routes-inspections.ts lines ~306 and ~427 use requireApproval
features.limits: It is a yes/no switch only. There are no approval thresholds (priority, cost, asset criticality), no approver routing by department, site or asset, and no multi-step approval. Nothing stops a supervisor approving a request they raised themselves (no segregation of duties). Approval does not create a work order automatically.

features.name: Raise a request (Report a fault)
features.what: Anyone with maintenance access raises a request; only the description is required (1 to 5000 characters). Optional: asset (must be in the company and not archived), priority (low, medium, high, urgent; default medium), department text or departmentId (departmentId for registered companies only), location, needed-by date, notes. Requests are numbered MR-0001 per company (mt_counters, which skip past any higher existing number). A search column is kept. Rate limit is 30 per minute per user. The form takes photos and documents, uploaded after the request is made, and warns about each one that fails.
features.evidence: POST /api/maintenance/c/:company/requests (routes-requests.ts); util.ts nextNumbers/NUMBERING; table mt_requests; client Requests.tsx RequestForm and NewRequestPage (route requests/new?assetId=); ReportFault.tsx modal opened from the module rail (components/layout/SuiteRail.tsx), which picks the company (localStorage bizomat-system-company, else a registered company, else the first) from GET /api/maintenance/companies; Field.tsx ScanPage links to requests/new?assetId=
features.limits: There is no request type or category field, no anonymous or public portal (a signed-in company member is required), no duplicate detection beyond showing the asset's open work orders to managers, no SLA or response-time target, and no acknowledgement email. Files are not uploaded in the same transaction as the request.

features.name: Request list and filters
features.what: Lists requests the caller may see. Filters: mine=1; status (open = submitted, awaiting_approval, approved, info_requested; awaiting = awaiting_approval or submitted; or a comma list of statuses); priority; assetId; from/to on the raised date (inclusive, UTC days); q (matches the request's or the asset's search text). Sort: newest (default), oldest, priority, number. limit up to 500, offset, total count. The screen has tabs Awaiting approval, Open, My requests and All for managers, and My requests and All I can see for others.
features.evidence: GET /api/maintenance/c/:company/requests (routes-requests.ts); client Requests.tsx RequestsPage (route requests)
features.limits: There is no paging control in the screen (it only says 'Showing X of Y'), no CSV export, no saved views, no department or site filter, and no filter by requester or decider.

features.name: Request detail and permissions
features.what: Returns the request (requestDTO) with: the asset's outstanding work orders (up to 50, managers only, for attaching); whether the caller can see the linked work order; comments; files; history (up to 200 events); the approval rule; and can.* flags for edit, approve, decline, requestInfo, respond, convert, attach, close, comment and upload. Edit (PATCH) is open to managers while the request is open, and to the requester while it is submitted, awaiting approval or info requested. Only changed fields are written, with a request.updated event holding before and after values.
features.evidence: GET and PATCH /api/maintenance/c/:company/requests/:id (routes-requests.ts loadRequest, columnsOf, validate); dto.ts requestDTO; client Requests.tsx RequestDetail and EditRequestDialog (route requests/:requestId)
features.limits: A technician who sees a request through their work order cannot comment on it or add files unless they raised it. There is no watchers list.

features.name: Request decisions: approve, decline, ask for information, respond, close
features.what: decide() makes a guarded status change (supervisor or above, only from the allowed statuses; a 409 if the status changed meanwhile). It sets decided_by and decided_at, writes an event and, optionally, a comment. Approve: from submitted, awaiting_approval or info_requested to approved, with an optional note. Decline: from those or approved to declined; the reason is required and kept as decision_note plus the comment 'Declined: ...'. Request info: from submitted, awaiting_approval or approved to info_requested; a comment is required. Respond: the requester (or a manager) answers with a comment and, optionally, a new description; the request goes back to awaiting_approval or submitted, following the rule. Close: from any status but closed, with an optional note; sets closed_at.
features.evidence: POST /requests/:id/approve, /decline, /request-info, /respond, /close (routes-requests.ts decide()); events request.approved, request.declined, request.info_requested, request.info_given, request.closed; client Requests.tsx action buttons and ReasonDialog
features.limits: Declined and closed are effectively final: there is no route to reopen or un-decline a request (a declined one can only be closed). Closing overwrites decided_by and decided_at with the closer, so 'Decided by' changes. The screen's Approve button sends no note, and Respond in the screen cannot change the description, although the server accepts both. Nobody is notified.

features.name: Request to work order: convert and attach
features.what: Convert (supervisor or above, request submitted, awaiting approval or approved, with no work order yet) makes a work order. The asset comes from the request or the body (one is required). Description, priority and department come from the request unless overridden; job type, technician, due dates, estimate, instructions, safety, trade, contractor, references, tasks and parts lines are accepted. The INSERT is guarded by 'request still has no work order', in the same transaction that sets the request to converted with work_order_id, so a request never becomes two work orders. Attach links the request to any outstanding work order of the company (status converted). A request belongs to one work order only; one work order can have many requests.
features.evidence: POST /requests/:id/convert and /requests/:id/attach (routes-requests.ts); routes-work.ts workOrderStatements(fromRequest) and fromRequestSchema; events request.converted, request.attached, work_order.created; client Requests.tsx ConvertDialog (asset, job type, priority, technician, due finish, estimated hours, instructions) and the 'Open work on this asset' Attach list
features.limits: There is no detach or move to another work order. The convert dialog does not offer trade, contractor, safety, due start, tasks, parts or department, although the server takes them. The attach screen lists only the request's asset's open work orders, so a request without an asset cannot be attached from the screen. Cancelling a work order leaves its requests at converted: they are not reopened or closed.

features.name: Requests made automatically
features.what: A failed prestart check raises one request: urgent if a critical item failed, otherwise medium, with its status set by the approval rule. A failed inspection whose template's fail_action is request raises one follow-up request; with fail_action work_order it makes a corrective work order instead. Both are guarded once-only by mt_done keys.
features.evidence: /home/user/bizomat-site/apps/work/src/worker/maintenance/routes-inspections.ts (prestart route ~line 415-440; inspection complete ~line 285-330); tables mt_prestarts, mt_wo_inspections, mt_done; client Field.tsx PrestartCheck result screen
features.limits: Follow-up work orders from inspections are made 'open' with no technician, no due date and no tasks.

features.name: Work order creation
features.what: Supervisor or above. Required: an asset (in the company and not archived) and a description. Optional: job type (corrective, preventive, breakdown, inspection, emergency_repair, electrical, mechanical, calibration, planned_shutdown, general), priority, department or departmentId, trade (free text, up to 80), assignedTo (must be a company person with technician role or above), contractor (free text), due start and due finish (finish not before start), estimated hours (stored as estimated_minutes), instructions, safety, project_ref, customer_ref, and initial tasks and parts lines (up to 100 each). Status is assigned when a technician is set, otherwise open. Numbered WO-00001.
features.evidence: POST /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders (routes-work.ts createSchema, columnsOf, validate, workOrderStatements); table mt_work_orders; client WorkOrders.tsx NewWorkOrderPage (route work-orders/new?assetId=)
features.limits: No standard-job or work order templates (only preventive templates, elsewhere), no sub-work orders or hierarchy, no budget or approval of the work order, no multiple assignees or crew, no contractor or supplier record (free text only), no linked purchase requisition, and no scheduling or calendar board. Trade is free text, not picked from mt_trades.

features.name: Work order list, filters and sorting
features.what: Lists work orders in scope. Filters: mine=1; status (outstanding = open, assigned, in progress, on hold; overdue = outstanding with due_finish before today; or a comma list); priority; jobType; trade (case-insensitive); assignedTo; assetId, with includeChildren=1 for the asset subtree (SUBTREE_SQL); dueFrom/dueTo; q (work order or asset search); siteId (inSiteSql). Sort: due (default), finish, number, priority, asset, jobType, created, status; dir asc or desc; limit up to 500. Also returns the company's distinct trades and today (taken from the client's date). The screen has tabs My work, Outstanding, Overdue and All, flags overdue rows and shows a 'Timer on' badge.
features.evidence: GET /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders (routes-work.ts SORTS, WO_SELECT with actual_minutes and my_timer subqueries); m2util.ts inSiteSql; util.ts todayFrom; client WorkOrders.tsx WorkOrdersPage
features.limits: The screen has no site or assignee filter (the server supports both), no paging control, no CSV, no bulk actions (assign, close) and no saved views.

features.name: Work order detail and editing
features.what: Detail returns: the work order (workOrderDTO with actualMinutes and timerRunning); the asset path; the number of other outstanding work orders on the asset (managers); linked requests; tasks; parts lines; labour lines with totals (actual, estimated, running timers, my timer); comments; files; history (up to 300); M2/M3 extras (inspections, stock moves, labour costs, costs, downtime, readings, preventive schedule); locked; and can flags for seeCosts, edit, work, complete, reopen, close and cancel. PATCH (supervisor or above, unlocked) changes any field. Setting a technician moves open to assigned; removing one moves assigned back to open. Only real differences are written (changes()), with event work_order.assigned or work_order.updated, guarded so the work order cannot be locked in the meantime.
features.evidence: GET and PATCH /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders/:id (routes-work.ts loadWorkOrder, updateSchema); routes-parts.ts workOrderExtras(); client WorkOrders.tsx WorkOrderDetail and EditWorkOrderDialog (route work-orders/:workOrderId)
features.limits: Technicians cannot edit the header (supervisors and above only). There is no change-reason prompt on edits and no record of reassignment history beyond the events.

features.name: Work order lifecycle and statuses
features.what: Statuses: open, assigned, in_progress, on_hold, completed, closed, cancelled. OUTSTANDING is the first four; LOCKED is completed, closed and cancelled. POST /status (assigned technician or manager, unlocked) moves to in_progress or on_hold with an optional note, which is also saved as a comment. Moving back to open or assigned is for managers only, and assigned needs a technician. Starting the timer moves open, assigned or on_hold to in_progress. Close (supervisor or above) moves completed to closed and sets closed_at. Cancel (supervisor or above, outstanding only, reason required) sets cancelled_at, stops and prices every running timer, adds the comment 'Cancelled: ...' and skips the preventive occurrence (pmCancelStmts). A locked work order refuses every change (assertUnlocked, 409) until it is reopened.
features.evidence: routes-work.ts POST /work-orders/:id/status, /close, /cancel, stopAllTimers, assertUnlocked; util.ts WO_STATUS, OUTSTANDING, LOCKED; pm.ts pmCancelStmts; client WorkOrders.tsx buttons Put on hold, Resume, Close, Cancel work order
features.limits: Close takes no note and the screen asks for no confirmation. There are no custom statuses, no 'waiting for parts' or 'waiting for contractor' status (on hold with a note only), no reason codes for on hold, and no automatic escalation of overdue work.

features.name: Completion
features.what: The assigned technician or a manager completes an outstanding work order. Completion notes are required (up to 10000). In one transaction it: sets completed, completion_notes, completed_at and completed_by; stops every running timer and prices those lines; completes every linked request still at converted (completed_at); writes events for the work order and each request; and moves any preventive schedule on (pmCompleteStmts, guarded on this completion).
features.evidence: POST /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders/:id/complete (routes-work.ts); routes-setup.ts priceLabourStmt; pm.ts pmCompleteStmts; client WorkOrders.tsx Complete dialog (ReasonDialog 'Completion notes')
features.limits: Completion does not require all tasks ticked, open inspections finished or downtime ended. There are no failure, cause or remedy codes, no signature or customer sign-off, and no separate supervisor verification step (close is optional). Completion does not change the asset's status and nobody is notified.

features.name: Reopening
features.what: Supervisor or above, on a locked work order, with a reason. Completed or closed work orders go back to in_progress; cancelled ones go back to assigned (if a technician is set) or open. It clears completed_at, completed_by, closed_at and cancelled_at, returns linked completed requests to converted, adds the comment 'Reopened: ...', writes a work_order.reopened event with the previous values plus request.reopened events, and makes the preventive occurrence outstanding again unless a newer one is (pmReopenStmts). The UPDATE is guarded on the work order still being locked.
features.evidence: POST /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders/:id/reopen (routes-work.ts); pm.ts pmReopenStmts; client WorkOrders.tsx Reopen dialog
features.limits: completion_notes are not cleared or versioned, so the old notes stay until the work order is completed again, and then they are overwritten. Labour costs and stock movements already recorded are kept. Closed requests are not reopened.

features.name: Tasks (checklist)
features.what: Tasks are text lines (up to 500 characters) on a work order, ordered by position. Initial tasks can be given on creation or convert. The assigned technician or a manager adds tasks, ticks and unticks them (done_at and done_by recorded) and edits task text, while the work order is unlocked. Only managers remove tasks. Every change is an event (task.added, task.done, task.undone, task.updated, task.removed). The screen shows 'Tasks (x of y done)' with who ticked each task and when.
features.evidence: POST /work-orders/:id/tasks, PATCH and DELETE /work-orders/:id/tasks/:taskId (routes-work.ts workable()); table mt_wo_tasks; client WorkOrders.tsx Tasks section
features.limits: There is no reorder route, no required or blocking tasks, no time or result per task, no task assignee and no task library. The screen cannot edit task text (the server allows it). Ticking tasks does not drive the work order status.

features.name: Required parts lines (text)
features.what: These are free-text part names with a quantity, listing what the job needs. They are added on creation, or by the assigned technician or a manager while unlocked. Lines can be changed and removed, with events part.added, part.updated and part.removed. This is separate from issuing real stock (parts issued and returned through ERP StockOps are under 'Parts used').
features.evidence: POST /work-orders/:id/parts, PATCH and DELETE /work-orders/:id/parts/:partId (routes-work.ts); table mt_wo_parts; client WorkOrders.tsx 'Required parts' section; stock issue in routes-parts.ts (/stock/issue, /stock/return)
features.limits: Lines are not linked to products, there is no reservation, and they are not used for cost. The screen offers add and remove only, not edit.

features.name: Labour timer
features.what: A start/stop timer per person per work order. Start: the assigned technician or a manager, unlocked work order; refused if the caller's timer is already running there (also enforced by the unique index mt_labour_running, mapped to a 409). It moves open, assigned or on_hold to in_progress with an event. Stop: the caller's own running timer; minutes are rounded from the elapsed time, the line is priced (entry timer) and the event labour.recorded is written. Complete and cancel stop every running timer. The overview lists the caller's running timers. The detail screen shows a live clock (useTick) and the time recorded against the estimate (a meter, with an over-estimate note).
features.evidence: POST /work-orders/:id/timer/start and /timer/stop (routes-work.ts); table mt_labour (ended_at NULL means running; unique partial index mt_labour_running); index.ts GET /overview myTimers; client WorkOrders.tsx timer card and Time section; Maintenance.tsx overview timer banner
features.limits: No pause and resume (stop and start again make a new line). A manager cannot stop someone else's timer except by completing or cancelling the work order. Timer lines cannot be edited or deleted. A person can run timers on several work orders at once. No GPS or clock-in.

features.name: Manual time entries
features.what: The assigned technician or a manager enters time by hand: a date (valid, not later than tomorrow UTC), minutes (1 to 1440), an optional note, and an optional userId (managers only, for a person with technician role or above). The line is stored in mt_labour (started at midnight UTC of the date) and priced at once (entry manual). Manual entries can be removed by their person or a manager (labour.removed). The screen's form takes hours and minutes, the date and 'For' (managers).
features.evidence: POST /work-orders/:id/labour and DELETE /work-orders/:id/labour/:labourId (routes-parts.ts); tables mt_labour, mt_labour_costs (entry = manual); client WorkOrderExtras.tsx LabourSection
features.limits: No start and end times of day, no overtime or rate types (normal, overtime, call-out), no timesheet approval, and no editing (remove and re-enter). Locked work orders refuse new entries and removals.

features.name: Trades and labour rates
features.what: Trades (mt_trades) have a unique name per company, an optional hourly rate in cents, and can be archived. Each person can have their own hourly rate (mt_technicians) and a set of trades (mt_technician_trades). Supervisors and above create and change these. Everyone can read the trades list, but rates and roles are shown only to managers. The work order list's trade filter uses the trades written on work orders.
features.evidence: GET and POST /api/maintenance/c/:company/trades, PATCH /trades/:id, PUT /technicians/:userId (routes-setup.ts); tables mt_trades, mt_technicians, mt_technician_trades; client Setup.tsx TradesSection (Settings page)
features.limits: Trades cannot be deleted (archive only). Rates have no effective dates or history (changes are logged only as events) and are a single currency in cents. A work order's trade is free text matched to mt_trades by name, so a typo gets no trade rate. Trades do not restrict who can be assigned.

features.name: Labour pricing and work order costs
features.what: Each labour line is priced once when its time is recorded, by priceLabourStmt into mt_labour_costs. The rate is the person's own rate, else the work order trade's rate (non-archived, matched by name), else the highest rate of the person's trades, else none. rate_source records which (person, work_order_trade, person_trade, or empty). Cost = round(minutes x rate / 60) cents, and NULL cost when there is no rate. Lines already priced are never repriced. The work order's costs (managers only) are labour cents, labour minutes without a rate, parts cents (from erp_stock_moves with source work_order) and the total. Per-line rate, source and cost are shown to managers. The asset costs report totals these per asset.
features.evidence: routes-setup.ts priceLabourStmt; routes-parts.ts workOrderExtras (labourCosts, costs, stock.financePosting); reports.ts costs report (GET /reports/costs, CSV); client WorkOrderExtras.tsx LabourSection ('Labour + parts = total') and PartsSection
features.limits: Costs are not posted to Finance ('Planned: ... posting it to Finance is not built yet'). There are no contractor, external or other cost lines, no budget or estimate cost against actual, no repricing after a rate change, and no costs shown to technicians or requesters.

features.name: Downtime
features.what: One downtime record per work order (mt_downtime, primary key company and work order) holding the asset, startedAt, endedAt (optional, so the asset can be 'down now') and cause. The assigned technician or a manager records or updates it while unlocked (PUT upsert, keeping the previous cause if none is given). Starts and ends cannot be more than 5 minutes in the future, and the end cannot be before the start. Only managers remove it. Events downtime.recorded and downtime.removed. It feeds the overview (assets down now) and the reliability and breakdowns reports (downtime, MTTR, MTBF, availability, for breakdown, emergency repair and corrective work orders).
features.evidence: PUT and DELETE /api/maintenance/c/:company/work-orders/:id/downtime (routes-parts.ts); table mt_downtime; index.ts overview assetsDownNow; reports.ts reliability and breakdowns; client WorkOrderExtras.tsx DowntimeSection ('Back up now' button)
features.limits: Only one downtime span per work order (no several stops), no downtime outside a work order, and no planned versus unplanned flag or production-loss value. features.name: Preventive maintenance schedules per asset (create, list, view, edit)
features.what: A supervisor or administrator creates a schedule on one asset. The trigger is time, meter or condition. The schedule also defines the work order it makes: name and description, job type (preventive or inspection), priority, tasks (up to 100 lines), required parts (up to 100 lines of part text and quantity), estimated hours (stored as minutes), lead days (0 to 365), trade, technician, inspection template, instructions, safety, and active. checkDefinition validates it: a time trigger needs an interval and a unit (day, week or month). A meter trigger needs a meter interval and a rising meter. A condition trigger needs a lower or upper limit, or a meter with an expected range, and the lower limit cannot be above the upper. The technician must be in the company and the inspection template must not be archived. initialState sets the first due point: for time, the start date or today, with anchor_day taken from that date. For meter, firstDueMeter, or else the meter's last_total plus the interval. The list filters by asset, template, site, active/paused, trigger and text, returns at most 500, and orders active first, then by next due. Each row includes the open work order, found through the occurrence with open_slot = 1. PATCH merges the changes and validates again. features.name: Time-based triggers (from completion or fixed dates)
features.what: A schedule comes due when date(next_due_date - lead_days) <= today. Completion basis: next_due_date stays put while the work order is open. When the work order is completed, the next date is the completion date (UTC) plus the interval. Fixed basis: the next date moves on when the work order is made. If the schedule is more than one occurrence behind, makeOccurrence jumps to the latest due date that has passed and records how many were skipped in the event summary. addInterval keeps the anchor day for monthly intervals (31 Jan, 28 Feb, 31 Mar). Changing startDate resets anchor_day, and also next_due_date if the schedule has never been done and has no open work order.

features.name: Meter-based triggers
features.what: A schedule comes due when the meter's life total (mt_meters.last_total) reaches next_due_meter. The occurrence key is m:<due meter>. The work order's due date is today plus lead days. Completion basis: next due = the meter total at completion (or else the due meter) plus the interval. Fixed basis: next due moves forward in whole intervals past the current total when the work order is made.

features.name: Condition-based triggers
features.what: A schedule comes due when the meter's latest reading (r.seq = m.last_seq) is below cond_below or above cond_above. Each limit falls back to the meter's expected_min/expected_max. It makes one work order per out-of-range reading (key c:<reading id>). It counts only readings taken after the last work order of the schedule was completed or cancelled. Its due date is today plus lead days. Cancelling or completing does not move any due state.

features.what: Every company route calls requireMt, which calls loadMtAccess(db, companyId, user). It tries three kinds of company in turn. gaps.rationale:
I checked the main claims in the code. Two things I found along the way matter for the design. First, the alerts table (erp_alerts), its helper and GET /x/alerts already exist, but no screen shows them. Second, StockOps.reserve and createRequisition exist but Maintenance does not call them.

Recommended release, in build order:

1. MX-01, notifications. This goes first because the later items send alerts through it: assignments to a crew, reservations that come up short, requisitions decided. It reuses erp_alerts and the email outbox, so it needs no new service or credential. Adding the bell also makes the module framework's existing alerts visible.
2. MX-02, the list filters, CSV and saved views. These are MEX's core listing features.
3. MX-04, the duplicate warnings. Small, and they touch the same request list rows as MX-02.
4. MX-03, asset details on the job. The job card needs it.
5. MX-05, the job card and PDF. It reuses the purchase order's PDF renderer.
6. MX-06, required parts linked to products. This turns the free-text lines into MEX's "parts listed on the job, issued from the job".
7. MX-07, reservations. Built on the MX-06 lines with the existing StockOps.reserve.
8. MX-08, requisitions from a job. It covers the shortfall that MX-06 and MX-07 show, using Procurement's own createRequisition and a side table. It keeps the ERP's own requisitions.raise right, so no permission decision is needed.
9. MX-09, the readings round. This is MEX's Readings Listing, and it reuses readingStatements and generateDue.
10. MX-10, labour by trade with a crew. It is the largest item and the one that changes visibility, so it goes last and can slip to the next release without breaking the others.

Together these cover MEX's standard work order end to end: find the job, see the asset, print it, plan the parts, reserve or buy them, issue them, record labour by trade, take readings, and tell people. One migration (0040) adds only nullable columns and side tables. No existing Maintenance, Procurement or Inventory table is rebuilt.

Next release, in order: MX-11 group work orders, then MX-12 inspection rounds with review. Rounds sit on groups and benefit from the crew model and the alerts, so they come after this release. After those: MX-13 the planning board, which needs MX-10's estimates by trade; MX-14 signatures; MX-15 recording work already done; MX-16 component codes and repeat failures; MX-17 cost codes; MX-18 contractors as suppliers. MX-26 corrects existing counts and can go in with MX-02.

Not buildable without the owner:
- MX-23, a portal for people without an account (unauthenticated input and privacy).
- MX-25, renaming labels and field security per group (design system and permission model).
- Posting any maintenance cost to Finance (which accounts to use).

Rules for every item in scope:
- Every new capability ships behind a flag that is off. Only the owner switches it on, under the Control Centre rule.
- Every new table goes into removeExample's list and passes the company_id query test.
- Existing example companies are not changed.
- The Knowledge Centre and docs/maintenance/README.md describe these only as built but off until the flags are on.
- Nothing from MEX's name, screens, text or data goes into the product.

A caution on the evidence: the MEX pages read are the mobile app guide. They do not show purchasing, a planner screen, budgets, warranties or fuel. So MX-08 and MX-13 are justified by the work order's parts requirement and its trade estimates, not by a MEX screen. I proposed nothing for budgets or warranties.

corrections.issue: The proposal misreads MEX's structure. In MEX a Work Order Inspection is one job that covers many assets, with one total-time display and one clock timer for the whole job, recorded under Trades. The proposal instead creates one child work order per asset. A 40-asset round would then show as 40 work orders in the listing, the dashboard counts and MX-01's overdue alerts (one per work order), and labour would be split across 40 jobs with no timer for the round. Separately, MEX only names the Exceptions and Not Approved filters. The pages read do not describe what they mean or who approves, so the segregation-of-duties review is BIZOMAT's own design, not MEX parity.

Add asset_id to mt_wo_inspections and widen UNIQUE (company_id, work_order_id, template_id) to include asset_id. mt_insp_results is keyed by inspection_id and needs no change, and follow_up_work_order_id / follow_up_request_id already sit on each inspection row, so follow-ups per asset carry over. Show progress, the timer and labour on that one job, so the listing shows one job as MEX does. Label 'Exceptions = failed items' and the supervisor review as BIZOMAT's own interpretation. MX-11 groups are then not needed for rounds.

corrections.issue: The evidence says GET /work-orders 'sorts like MEX', but it does not. In routes-work.ts SORTS, 'due' sorts by due_finish and 'finish' sorts by completed_at. There is no sort by due start, and dueFrom/dueTo filter on due_finish only. MEX sorts by Due Date (due start) and Due Finish Date separately and filters on Date Due Start. The proposal adds raised and finished date filters but no due-start filter or sort.
corrections.correct: Add a due-start sort and dueStartFrom/dueStartTo filters (both columns already exist in mt_work_orders), keep the due-finish sort, and relabel 'Finish date' as 'Completed'. Then the list really has MEX's Due Date, Due Finish Date and Date Due Start.

(3) MEX emails 'the people who must approve it'. The proposal emails every supervisor and admin, and BIZOMAT has no list of designated approvers (approve only checks requireMt 'supervisor').
corrections.correct: Record the email-approval omission as a deliberate departure, or as a decision for the owner. Add 'linked work order cancelled' to the requester's alerts (see the missed item). Say that approvers are all supervisors and admins until per-department or per-site approvers exist.

missed.feature: What happens to a request when its work order is cancelled
missed.mexModule: Job Requests (Requests Listing: outstanding excludes requests attached to a closed or cancelled Work Order)
missed.note: Not covered by any gap. The cancel route (routes-work.ts, POST /work-orders/:id/cancel) never touches mt_requests. A converted request stays 'converted' forever, pointing at a cancelled work order, and the requester is never told. MX-02's new 'outstanding' rule would just drop it from the list with no final status. Proposal: in the same batch as the cancel, move linked converted requests to a resolved status (back to approved for a new work order, or closed with the cancel reason as a comment), write an event, and alert the requester through MX-01.

missed.mexModule: Job Requests (statuses: cancelled is separate from declined)
missed.note: MEX has a 'cancelled' request status separate from 'declined'. BIZOMAT has no cancelled status: the mt_requests status CHECK in 0018 is submitted, awaiting_approval, approved, declined, info_requested, converted, completed, closed. Only a supervisor can close a request (routes-requests.ts /close uses decide(), which needs the supervisor role). A requester who raised a duplicate or no longer needs the work cannot withdraw it. Low effort: let the requester withdraw while it is submitted, awaiting_approval or info_requested, with a reason, recorded as closed with an event, or with a new status in a migration.

missed.feature: Reading Types as a shared list (usage-based or condition monitoring)
missed.note: MEX needs a Reading Type on every reading (for example Exhaust Temperature or Operating Hours) and classes readings as usage-based or condition monitoring. In BIZOMAT, meters belong to each asset with a free-text name, a unit and a rising flag (mt_meters, 0024), and there is no 'kind' column, although MX-09 assumes one. With no shared types, MX-09's round cannot be filtered by reading type and MX-20's trend cannot compare one type across assets. Possible fix: a per-company list of reading types (name, unit, usage or condition), with an optional reading_type_id on mt_meters and a round filter by type.
